solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Event in Met and NHS departments

parts.note: taken as written
the Criminal Investigation Department is a branch of the Metropolitan Police
Ear, Nose and Throat is a hospital department in the NHS, Britain's National Health Service

explanation.surface: Something has happened that involves both the London police and hospital departments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police; read 'departments' as covering both, one from the police and one from the NHS.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an occurrence or happening, a close synonym for an event.

clue.text: Fish that's stuffed with diamonds

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with filling has something packed inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A luxurious fish dish with jewels packed inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' expands to 'that is', abbreviated as i.e.; the suit letter goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater carp-family species, also called the orfe, much loved by setters.

clue.text: Verify clubs working with company

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a machine that is working is on
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: An auditor checks a golf club's accounts with the help of an outside company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' reads like golf or social clubs, but it is the card suit, reduced to its single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to establish that it is true, the same as checking or verifying it.

clue.text: One of the Queen's dedicated lovers?

definitions.text: One of the Queen's dedicated lovers?

parts.words: One of the Queen's dedicated lovers?
parts.note: surface reading: a devoted admirer of the British monarch
setter's reading: the queen is a queen bee, and the males of the hive exist only to mate with her

explanation.walkthrough: The capital Q pushes you towards royalty; the queen is in a beehive, and her suitors are male bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A male honeybee has no sting and gathers no nectar; its sole purpose is mating with the hive's queen.

clue.text: Common brown climbing flower

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ural runs through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A garden description: an ordinary brown flowering climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing flower' looks like a plant such as clematis, but 'flower' is a river, a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural can mean normal or ordinary, as in a natural reaction, matching common in its sense of usual.

clue.text: Horse around in sarong on vacation

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it
a vacated place is emptied, so only its outer shell remains

parts.note: the word with its interior cleared out
ca. abbreviates circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: Someone fooling about while wearing a sarong on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse around' looks like a phrase meaning fool about, but 'Horse' alone is the definition, slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both horse and scag are street slang names for the drug heroin.

clue.text: I can't be shifting display case

indicators.note: things that are shifting are moved about into new positions

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A removal man complains he cannot be the one to move a heavy display case.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase before 'shifting' is the fodder; reading 'I can't be shifting' as a complaint hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, often glass-fronted for showing off ornaments or china.

clue.text: Insect, one of ten on the wall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a metallic green blowfly

definitions.text: one of ten on the wall?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an item from a British children's counting song in which ten of them hang on a wall and fall one by one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten Green Bottles' is a British children's counting-down song in which bottles hanging on a wall accidentally fall one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The fly is named for its shiny green body; the song's bottles are literally green bottles.

clue.text: Mountain housing a wind generator

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it within its walls

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A turbine installed on a mountain top, harnessing the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind generator' suggests a turbine; the joke is that beans are notorious for causing flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating beans is famously said to cause intestinal gas, a humorous rather than dictionary description.

clue.text: Bet better than badly bloated mug

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, leaving the letters in a mess

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler boasts of beating a puffed-up fool at wagering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to have bet better than someone is to have beaten them at gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgamble a rival is to beat them at wagering, so the past tense matches 'bet better than'.

clue.text: Country song about male lovers

indicators.note: to go about something is to go round it, enclosing it

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
lovers who are male are men

explanation.surface: A country-and-western ballad about men in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' pulls towards country music, but 'Country' stands alone as the definition and 'song' is the opera word.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus, bordering Turkey, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Iran.

clue.text: Pound of tea and coffee picked up?

indicators.note: a sound picked up is caught by the ear, as a microphone picks up voices

parts.note: tea and coffee are both brewed drinks, hence brews

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a pound weight of tea and coffee to take home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the weight or money but is the verb, to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bruise is to crush or batter, as when you pound garlic in a mortar or fruit gets damaged.

clue.text: Understanding a relation is tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is devious, so the letters are set out deceptively

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Family life: getting on with a relative can be hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb of the sentence but belongs to the fodder; British spelling uses -isation.
explanation.definitionFit: A realisation is the moment of coming to grasp or comprehend something, a form of understanding.

clue.text: Possibly neat drink swallowed by worker

parts.note: rum is a spirit
what is swallowed by something ends up in it
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A spirit drunk straight, knocked back by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' suggests an undiluted drink, but it is an old word for cattle; the wordplay is read literally as drink 'in' worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for oxen or cattle, which chew the cud, so a neat is an example of this animal group.

clue.text: Black's Tal? Ignore opening and just castle!

indicators.note: to ignore the opening is to leave out the first letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades and chess notation; the possessive simply joins it to the next piece
the chess grandmaster's name without its first letter
a just person is upright and moral

explanation.surface: Chess advice: Mikhail Tal, playing black, should skip the opening theory and simply castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal was a Latvian world chess champion; 'castle' is the chess move in the surface but a royal residence in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is the British royal family's private Scottish residence in Aberdeenshire, a castle by name and structure.

clue.text: See trip abroad as this?

indicators.note: abroad means widely scattered, so the letters are spread out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a holiday overseas should be seen as a welcome break.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a trip abroad is a break from routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or relief from something difficult, which a holiday overseas provides.

clue.text: No, don't start helping people

indicators.note: read as 'no do at the start', telling you to drop a two-letter verb from the front

parts.note: a donation is a gift that helps a cause

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to begin assisting the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as refusing help; split 'don't' into 'do not' and the instruction is to remove DO from the start of the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people, a large community sharing history, language or territory.

clue.text: Musical compositions from Kings?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: kings are examples of chessmen, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests music from King's College, Cambridge, famous for its choir; the question mark flags kings as examples of chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical work, and kings, queens and pawns are all pieces on a chessboard.

clue.text: Cold actor picks up cap in military town

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a cap is a type of hat
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A performer with a chill grabs a cap while in a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the actor picking up the cap holds it above himself, so the cap's letters sit before his.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatham in Kent was home to a Royal Navy dockyard and remains the base of the Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Game plans you've eavesdropped on

indicators.note: eavesdropping is listening in, so what is meant is what you hear

parts.note: drafts are preliminary plans or sketches

explanation.surface: Someone has overheard your secret tactics for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for the board game Americans call checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts is a two-player board game played with flat round counters on a chequered board.

clue.text: Sponge, gutted darter and octopus?

indicators.note: a gutted fish has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside

parts.note: the word with its middle cleared out
an octopus squirts ink, so it is playfully an inker; the question mark flags the invented word

explanation.surface: A list of sea creatures: a sponge, a cleaned-out darter fish and an octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: The marine surface makes 'Sponge' look like the sea animal; it is the definition, a heavy boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponge is informal for someone who soaks up alcohol, a heavy tippler.

clue.text: Accommodation housing one rare English animal

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it within its walls

parts.note: gaff is British slang for a person's home
the Roman numeral for one
R is an abbreviation for rare
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A lodging that shelters a single unusual English creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaff is informal British for a house or flat; it holds the numeral and the abbreviation, and the language letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an African mammal, the tallest living land creature, with a very long neck.

clue.text: Treat angina in religious Bow man

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, religious

indicators.note: to treat something is to process it, working it into a different form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor treating chest pain in a devout man from Bow, in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow looks like the London district, but a bow is what a violinist plays with.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was a celebrated Italian violin virtuoso, and a violinist wields a bow.

clue.text: Waits on others as becomes a man!

parts.note: straight reading: attends to other people's needs at table or in service
setter's flourish: helping others is presented as the manly, honourable thing to do

explanation.walkthrough: The plain sense carries the clue; the exclamation adds a moral tag about duty, without separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends to diners or masters is said to serve them, as a waiter or butler does.

clue.text: Chair in an American saloon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an enclosed seat carried on poles by two bearers
second meaning: the US word for a saloon car

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a Wild West bar with chairs in it, but it is the British word for a family car with a separate boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was carried by two bearers, and Americans call a four-door enclosed car by the same name.

clue.text: Description of 20 shirts can be so

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what you would say of the long-necked animal at 20
second meaning: a garment with a collar that comes up the throat

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the tall animal at 20-down, whose neck reaches high.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe's neck rises far above its body, and a garment cut up to the throat is described the same way.

clue.text: Bit of dope?

parts.note: surface reading: a small quantity of cannabis
setter's reading: dope is slang for information, so a bit of it is a single piece of truth

explanation.walkthrough: Dope as slang for inside information (getting the dope on someone) is the key; the drugs reading is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope means information or the inside story, and one item of true information is a single datum.

clue.text: Animal whip

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nine-thonged naval lash once used for flogging, known by its short name

explanation.walkthrough: The naval cat-o'-nine-tails is routinely shortened to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A feline pet is a mammal, and the short name of the knotted flogging lash is the same word.

clue.text: One sought by the cops about electronic tag

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: police hunting a suspect say they want a man, as in a manhunt
e- is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A wanted criminal is tracked down by the police via an ankle monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic tag' reads as one phrase, the offender's ankle device, but it splits: one letter of wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag can be a label or identifier, as in a name tag, so it serves as what someone is called.

clue.text: New parents close to font here?

definitions.text: New parents close to font here?

indicators.note: something made new is remade, its parts put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: New parents stand near the baptismal font at a christening in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a church area where parents might gather by the font.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is the crosswise arm of a cruciform church, a part of the building where a font may stand.
